summary: Full backend (Micronaut/Java + H2 + JWT) and frontend (React /signup, /login, session, logout) testing for Kindred Wealth. Backend: 20/20 pytest tests pass (health, signup, validation, login, /api/me, role enforcement on /api/customers, self/admin access on /api/customers/{id}, PATCH onboarding updates, JWT persistence across backend restart). Frontend: 2-step signup → dashboard, login (wrong + correct creds), session persistence on reload, user-menu logout, and protected-route redirect all working. Fixed environment blocker: Java JRE was missing from the container so the backend supervisor was in FATAL state (502 on /api/health); installed openjdk-17-jre-headless and the backend started cleanly.

minor.issue: Backend silently lowercases email on storage (canonicalisation). Tests written with mixed-case TEST_ prefix initially failed; behavior is fine but should be documented and the signup response should reflect the canonical (lowercased) value (it already does). Frontend already lowercases before submit, so OK.

issues: Multiple console warnings: 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' from Recharts ResponsiveContainer when parent layout is briefly 0x0 on mount. Cosmetic only — charts render correctly after layout settles.

action_items: Note for deploy/runbook: container needs a JRE 17 on PATH for the supervisor command `/usr/bin/java ... -jar backend-0.1.jar`. Without it the backend goes into FATAL with 'can't find command /usr/bin/java'. Either bake openjdk-17-jre-headless into the base image or pin the supervisor command to a vendored JDK so a forked env survives.
Optional polish: add minWidth/minHeight (or fixed height) to Recharts ResponsiveContainer parents to silence width(-1)/height(-1) warnings on first mount.
Optional UX: consider adding an explicit `data-testid="logout-button"` on the Sign out menu item (currently discoverable only via `user-menu-trigger` → text 'Sign out').
critical_code_review_comments: Auth flow: bcrypt + JWT (HS256, 2h), Authorization: Bearer enforcement, 401/403 split, and self-vs-admin authorization on /api/customers/{id} all behave per spec.
Validation: 400 on short password (<8) and missing fullName confirmed; 409 with {error:'email_taken'} on duplicate signup confirmed.
JWT persistence: token issued before `supervisorctl restart backend` continues to validate after restart (H2 file DB + fixed JWT_SECRET in supervisor env). Confirmed end-to-end via /api/me.

Frontend session: localStorage `wm_session` stores {token,user{id,fullName,email,phone,country,dateOfBirth,role,createdAt}}; on reload `auth.jsx` revalidates via /api/me and keeps the user signed in. Logout clears the key and protected routes redirect to /login. Verified.
Env hygiene: frontend uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL only; backend reads JWT_SECRET / ADMIN_EMAIL / ADMIN_PASSWORD / H2_FILE from supervisor env. No hardcoded secrets in code.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (created — 20 pytest cases covering all auth + onboarding scenarios)
Installed openjdk-17-jre-headless system package so supervisor can launch the Micronaut jar (otherwise backend was in FATAL state).
test_credentials: ADMIN admin@kindred.local / Admin@12345 (auto-seeded). Customers: created on the fly via POST /api/auth/signup with unique lowercase emails (e.g. test_*@kindred.test).
seed_data_creation: Each test run creates ~6 throwaway CUSTOMER accounts via /api/auth/signup (lowercase TEST_-style prefixes). Not cleaned up because no admin DELETE endpoint exists; fine for H2 file DB. To reset: rm /app/backend/data/kindred.* && sudo supervisorctl restart backend.
context_for_next_testing_agent: If the backend returns 502 on /api/health, first run `which java`; if missing, `apt-get install -y openjdk-17-jre-headless && sudo supervisorctl restart backend`. Backend takes ~5s to come up. Use lowercase emails when asserting equality (server normalises). Logout is reached via [data-testid=user-menu-trigger] → text 'Sign out'. Portfolio data (assets/transactions/goals) is still localStorage-mocked and out of scope.
rca of the issue: Initial 502 on /api/health was not a code bug. The forked container shipped without a JRE so supervisor could not exec `/usr/bin/java`. Backend status was FATAL with 'can't find command /usr/bin/java'. Fix: `apt-get install -y openjdk-17-jre-headless` then `sudo supervisorctl restart backend`. Health 200 within ~5s of restart; all 20 backend tests pass. Long-term mitigation: bake JDK17 into the base image or vendor it so a supervisor-managed Micronaut app survives env forks.
